title: Coordinated client retry handling and partial-output compaction for disconnected streams
creator: Ethan Chen
description: Problem: client disconnects, sudden timeouts, or flaky networks frequently leave partial model outputs (generation blobs) on the server. These artifacts: 1) consume KV and ephemeral storage; 2) complicate resume semantics and KV-cache reconciliation; 3) leak cost; and 4) make client retries ambigious (duplicate continuation vs. fresh generation). This ticket designs coordinated client retry semantics and a compaction/GC scheme for partial-output blobs that preserves resume friendliness, makes retries idempotent, and bounds resource usage.
background: We've observed repeated incidents where sessions with slow networks disconnect and the platform retains partial outputs for long TTLs. Existing heuristics in ENG-101234 provide resume tokens, but they are not robust to concurrent client retries or long tail disconnects. Related incidents: PROD-2025-11-07 streaming-orphan-surge and spike in ephemeral storage usage reported on grafana/streams-ephemeral-storage.
goals: 1) Define a canonical client retry protocol with an explicit retry coordinator token that prevents duplicate continuation runs. 2) Implement server-side partial-blob compaction that merges small partial fragments, summarizes progress, and enforces compact GC. 3) Add observability and SLIs: orphaned-partial-count, partial-compactions/sec, resume-success-rate. 4) Provide migration plan and compatibility for older clients.
non_goals: Full rework of streaming protocol, changing wire format for streaming deltas, or modifying user-facing SDK APIs in this phase.
proposal_overview: Introduce a lightweight Retry Coordination header (X-Redwood-Retry-ID) that is generated by client SDKs on a user-visible request attempt and carried through retries. On the server: 1) treat a Retry-ID as an idempotency key for a top-level generation; 2) maintain a small RetryRegistry with epoch fencing; 3) write periodic compact checkpoints for partial outputs (every 512 tokens or on fragment count>5) into compressed partial blobs. Compaction merges fragments and emits a compacted checkpoint with a monotonic sequence number. GC policy: compacted partials kept for 30 minutes after last client activity; un-compacted fragments cleaned after short TTL (90s).
design_decisions:
- Retry-ID is client-supplied to keep server stateless for new attempts. Server validates and returns a canonical RetryToken that contains a server-epoch to prevent cross-node duplicate continuations.
- Partial blobs are stored as compressed LZ4 frames referencing KV cache cursors; compaction rewrites blobs to include only essential prefix and latest KV cursor.
- Compaction is opportunistic: triggered on write path by threshold or by background compactor process to avoid synchronous latency impact.
- Resume flow: client presents Retry-ID and optionally last-seen sequence number. Server validates canonical epoch and serves compacted prefix plus resumes generation from KV cursor position.
- Backpressure interplay: clients that flood with retries without exponential backoff will be rate-limited by the existing per-client token bucket. Compaction reduces memory pressure but is not a substitute for rate limiting.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Retry-ID header accepted and round-tripped by SDKs; server deduplicates duplicate attempts within 5 minutes with <1% false-positive rate.
2) Partial compaction reduces average partial-fragment-count by >=60% under experiment traffic in staging.
3) Resume success rate >= 99.5% for resumed generations in canary.
4) Observability: graphs for orphaned-partial-count, compacted-bytes, resume-success-rate available in Console dashboard.
5) Unit and integration tests covering race conditions (simultaneous retry from two clients, node failover during compaction).
implementation_steps: API: Add X-Redwood-Retry-ID header support in gateway and SDKs (JS/Python/Go).
Server: Implement RetryRegistry with TTL and server-epoch tokens.
Storage: Add partial-blob compaction storage schema and LZ4 compression utility.
Compactor: Background compaction worker and thresholds (token count, fragment count).
Resume: Enhance resume handshake to accept Retry-ID + last-seq and return compaction metadata.
GC: Implement two-tier GC: fast TTL for fragments (90s) and longer TTL for compactions (30m).
Observability: add metrics and Console dashboard panels.
Rollout: Feature-flagged rollout: start in staging, then canary in dedicated cluster, then gradual host rollout.

test_plan:
- Unit tests for RetryRegistry epoch transitions and fencing.
- Integration test: simulate two clients simultaneously retrying with same Retry-ID; assert single authoritative generation and correct resume.
- Stress test: generate 10k short streaming requests with flaky disconnects and compare fragment counts with baseline.
- Chaos test: node kill during compaction; assert no corruption and eventual consistent resume.
- SDK E2E: JS and Python SDKs must round-trip Retry-ID and handle server canonical token responses.
observability_and_slos: Add new SLIs: resume-success-rate (target>=99.5%), orphan-partial-count (target < 0.05 per active session), partial-compaction-byte-saved. Alerting: fire P1 on resume-success-rate < 99% for 5 minutes in production canary. Dashboards: streaming/partial-compaction and streaming/retry-coordinator.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag default off. 1) Enable in staging cluster for 48h. 2) Canary-enable on 5% of hosted traffic with monitoring. 3) Expand to 25% after 24h if SLOs stable. 4) Full rollout after 7 days and postmortem-free canary. Provide SDK migration note for clients to adopt Retry-ID for better resume UX.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Retry-ID header can be spoofed by intermediate proxies. Mitigation: gateway will issue a server-canonical token (signed) and reject unverified cross-node retries.
Risk: Compaction may add I/O and increase tail-latency. Mitigation: make compaction async; background worker with IO backoff and per-node IO budget.
Risk: Older clients that do not send Retry-ID may get treated as unique attempts. Mitigation: default server behavior remains compatible; we only dedupe when Retry-ID present.
Risk: Misconfigured GC could prematurely delete resumable state. Mitigation: keep safety delta (compaction TTL + 2x max retry window) and add metric to detect resume-failures correlated with GC.
open_questions: 1) Should we version the Retry-ID semantics as part of protocol header to allow future extension? 2) What is the canonical TTL for RetryRegistry for cross-region retries? Proposal: 5 minutes but needs legal review for long-running regulated sessions. 3) Should compaction emit an audit log entry for compliance requirements?
next_steps: 1) Finish gateway passthrough PR and land runtime RetryRegistry. 2) Stabilize compaction worker and add chaos-test coverage. 3) Coordinate SDK release (minor) to add Retry-ID generation. 4) Create console dashboard and alerting rules before any canary.
